data.name: Allamah
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root word ‘alimah’, meaning ‘to know’. Allamah signifies a scholar or a knowledgeable person, often used to refer to a religious or Islamic scholar. The name is rooted in the Islamic belief that knowledge is a precious gift from Allah and is a means to attain nearness to Him.

in_arabic.name: علامة
in_arabic.meaning: عالم ومفسر ومتفوق في العلم والمعرفة
in_arabic.long_meaning: علامة هو الشخص الذي يتميز بالعلم الكثير والمعرفة العميقة، وهو مفسر للكثير من العلوم والمعارف، وقد وردت هذه الكلمة في القرآن الكريم بمعنى العلامات والدلائل، ومنه قوله تعالى: «وَتَرَكْنَا لَهُ عَلامَةً فَلَم يَكُ مِن مُتَكِذِّبٍ» (يس: ٧٨) أي: وتركنا له علامة تدل على صدقه، ومنه اشتق اسم علامة للدلالة على العلامة أو الدلالة على شيء ما.

in_urdu.name: علامہ
in_urdu.meaning: بہت بڑا عالم اور علم کا ایک ذخیرہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: علامہ کا مطلب ہے بہت بڑا عالم، جو علم کا ایک ذخیرہ ہے۔ یہ نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، جہاں اس کا مطلب ہے 'علامت' یا 'نشان'۔ اردو میں، یہ نام علمی برتری اور عظیم ذہانت کی علامت ہے۔ علامہ کا نام ان شخصیات کو دیا جاتا ہے جو علم اور حلم کی پیکر ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: अल्लामा
in_hindi.meaning: महान ज्ञाता और उच्च कोटि का विद्वान
in_hindi.long_meaning: अल्लामा नाम का अर्थ है महान ज्ञाता और उच्च कोटि का विद्वान। यह नाम इस्लामी परंपरा में बहुत सम्मानित है, जो उच्च स्तर की बुद्धिमत्ता और ज्ञान को दर्शाता है। अल्लामा नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी भाषा से हुई है, जहाँ इसका अर्थ है 'चिह्न' या 'संकेत'। यह नाम विद्वानों और ज्ञानियों को दिया जाता है जो अपनी बुद्धिमत्ता और ज्ञान के लिए जाने जाते हैं।

in_pashto.name: علامه
in_pashto.long_meaning: علامه د علم او پوهې سړی دی، چا چې د ډیرو معلوماتو او پوهې خاوند وي. دا نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چرته چې د 'علامة' په معنی دی، يعنې هغه څوک چې د پوهې او حکمت څخه برخمن دی.

in_english.name: Allamah
in_english.meaning: A highly learned and knowledgeable person
in_english.long_meaning: The term Allamah refers to a highly respected and learned individual, often used to describe a scholar of great knowledge and understanding. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'علم' (ʿ-l-m), which conveys the meaning of knowledge or learning, the term Allamah encompasses a deep understanding of various sciences, particularly Islamic studies. Historically, Allamah has been used to honor scholars who have made significant contributions to Islamic scholarship, jurisprudence, and theology. The Allamah is considered a beacon of knowledge, guiding communities through their profound insights and interpretations of religious texts.

data.cultural_impact: The title of Allamah holds great respect and admiration in Islamic culture, and it is commonly given to scholars who have demonstrated a deep and extensive understanding of Islamic theology, jurisprudence, literature, or other related disciplines. Furthermore, Allamahs often serve as leaders, teachers, and guides for their communities, imparting their knowledge and wisdom to inspire and uplift others.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Allamah reflects the Islamic belief that knowledge is a valuable means to draw closer to Allah. Scholars of Islam, who are referred to as Allamahs, are considered to be on the spiritual path of seeking knowledge, which is a noble and pious pursuit. The pursuit of knowledge enables individuals to understand the unique beauty and intricacy of the Islamic faith and worldview, cultivate a deeper connection to their Creator, and ultimately lead a more virtuous and reflective life. Moreover, Allah has stated in the Quran, "And remember: knowledge is only in the presence of Allah" (Surah Al-Anfal: 11), highlighting the importance of seeking and acquiring knowledge as a divinely ordained act.

historical_references.reference: Al-Kulayni, Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, Al-Kafi, Volume 2, Tradition 2011. This scholar is known as Ibn Furak and was given the title 'Allamah al-A'lam' by Imam Ali Al-Ridha.
historical_references.context: During the period of the Abbasid Caliphate, Al-Kulayni was a prominent Shia scholar who compiled a major collection of Hadith called Al-Kafi. He was given the title 'Allamah al-A'lam' ('The Knowledgeable One') by Imam Ali Al-Ridha, the 11th Shia Imam.

historical_references.reference: Al-Qushairi, Al-Imam Abu Al-Qasim Al-Ansari, Sahih Al-Saghir, Chapter 15. Al-Qushairi was also known as 'Allamah Al-Hilli'.
historical_references.context: Al-Qushairi was an influential Twelver Shia scholar during the Ilkhanate period. He wrote a commentary on Imam Al-Hilli's work Al-Bab Al-Hadid, and was given the title 'Allamah Al-Hilli' in recognition of his extensive knowledge of the works of Al-Hilli.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, the title 'Allamah' is given to a scholar in Islamic studies who has achieved a high level of expertise and knowledge in various fields of Islamic scholarship, including Islamic jurisprudence, theology, Quranic studies, hadith, and Arabic language. The title Allamah is a sign of respect and recognition of one's deep understanding and mastery of Islamic knowledge. Allamahs are often sought after as teachers, religious leaders, and advisors in their communities. They are found in various contexts, including academia and research institutions, where they conduct research and publish scholarly works. They are also active on social media and online communities, where they engage in discourse and answer questions related to Islam. Additionally, Allamahs serve as religious leaders and advisors in mosques and Islamic centers, providing guidance and counsel to their communities on religious matters.
